requires: the engine's own state folder; commands that change state take the exclusive product lock

commands.effect: lists every engine pair; changes nothing
adds a switched-on pair after checking that the local folder exists and the account loads; no file is touched

verifies current root identities against the old pair, then copies its definition and saved baseline into the engine, keeping its exclusions and first-run checks; reports source, imported and discarded stale-folder counts; no endpoint file is touched

removes the exact pair and eligible saved records only when the shared recovery/custody guards permit it; unresolved pending effects, stages or in-flight work refuse removal without erasing evidence; no file is touched
switches the pair on so Repair can run it
switches the pair off; a switched-off pair is never repaired
without --yes shows what the next Repair would copy first and remove, and where it can be recovered, changing nothing; with --yes adds the exclusion; --keep excludes without removing anything
removes the exclusion while preserving saved sync history and first-Repair state; the next Repair uses that history, including remembered deletions

binds freshly checked roots for an unbound exact pair; an existing binding must match both saved identities, and a matching check closes its exact root notice without changing generation or source obligations; preserves sync history and recovery custody; does not approve replacement or missing roots, list files or run Repair
starts or attaches to the current Engine host through verified readiness; closing a window does not stop the Engine host

shows the current Engine host's actual work phase, waiting reason and last reported progress, watching, session-only pauses or unavailable state; starts no host and changes nothing; responsiveness is not proof of progress
pauses new dispatch and drains admitted work for the exact pair, or globally when --pair is omitted; acquisition continues; pause is session-only and ends when the Engine host restarts

clears the exact pair's session-only pause, or the global pause when --pair is omitted; global pause still dominates pair resume, and global resume preserves explicit pair pauses; resume alone does not retry in-use items
safely stops the current Engine host and its reused supervisor, drains admitted work, checkpoints and joins owned resources; closing a window does not perform this stop; never forces termination

reads both sides in full and syncs the pair; progress goes to standard error, including periodic listing counts during direct Repair. Windows-invalid Dropbox names are skipped with the existing SkipReservedName notice, without name substitution; saved bindings and local copies are preserved, and a skip is not deletion authority. --show-files adds per-action cards to the human progress; the run log always records every committed effect
shows one stored run log as readable text, changing nothing; the raw log file keeps its six-column machine format. An unfinished trailing record is ignored and malformed records are reported
shows each pair's last Repair, open notices and exclusions; changes nothing

lists the pair's active notices grouped by cause, with counts; --ignored lists hidden, non-dismissed notices with Restore. Changes nothing. Shows definite in-use or ambiguous in-use-or-access-denied diagnoses truthfully; retries wait for that file's real change/CLOSE, the next Repair or user Retry, with no timed-item retry or countdown and no promise that an unchanged close emits a journal record. Windows-invalid Dropbox names use the existing Skipped/SkipReservedName notice without substitution; rename them in Dropbox to sync them

applies a choice only to the exact reviewed notice version from engine issues; --reviewed is required with --issue and forbidden with --all. A replaced notice refuses the stale choice without effects; ignore hides it and unignore restores it without resolving the problem, releasing holds or changing retry work. Visibility choices reject --name, --rules, --first-run and --all. --all is only for retry and reports retried and succeeded counts without a single issue ID. Item retries sync only the subject paths, or the notice path when no subjects were observed. Prerequisite retries use the automatic prerequisite route; only outstanding Repair debt runs Repair. Dismiss keeps an ignored-content folder this time; keep-folder-always requires one exact issue and nonempty --rules, no --all/--name/--first-run, and atomically saves covered keep preferences and dismisses that notice without Repair or provider effects. First-sync resets history under exact authority while preserving root binding and recovery custody; sync-normally retains history. Neither choice approves missing roots or replays uncertain effects. Bind-roots checks and binds an unbound pair, or closes its exact root notice only if the saved identities still match; matching bindings preserve source cursors and obligations

lists active local and folder recovery operations without --operation, with --after-operation for listing continuation; with --operation shows exact evidence and all known paths in pages using --after. Reports provenance, custody, generations, allowed choices and uncertainty; inspection changes nothing and never replays effects

resolves only the exact recovery operation and generation; folder-member actions also require exact item and item-generation. Every choice requires --yes. Check reconciles qualified evidence without replaying uncertain effects; accept-current acknowledges current or unknown recovery without claiming historical success; abandon-incoming discards only verified owned incoming stages, never current occupants or remote bytes. Legacy or unknown-ownership locators require manual handling; terminal operation acknowledgement preserves honest uncertainty and requires settled custody and joined jobs; no --all or force
Lists the exact pair's stored additional ignore rules, or its keep-folder preferences with --folder-keep; changes nothing. Engine defaults apply only to ignore scope, not keep preferences.

Replaces the exact pair's additional ignore rules, or with --folder-keep its future keep-folder preferences. None clears only the selected list, never the other list or engine defaults. Keep preferences do not widen ignore scope or authorize deletion, and editing them does not dismiss notices. Applies on the next Repair; no files are touched now. Removing an ignore-scope rule can make existing changes and deletions eligible again; removing a keep preference can restore future keep notices, never deletion authority. Syntax: FileExtension:value, FileName:value, FolderName:value, or FileNamePrefix:value; separate rules with semicolons.

lists every engine setting, its value and whether you changed it; works before any pair exists. Includes LogBufferCharacters, the log buffer size in characters, and the read buffers LogReadBufferBytes (log view read chunk, bytes) and JournalPageBufferBytes (one USN journal page, bytes), through this existing settings command

changes one engine setting in your settings file, including LogBufferCharacters as a positive Int32 character count, LogReadBufferBytes as a positive Int32 byte count and JournalPageBufferBytes as at least one native USN record page; no separate logging command
reads the current user's existing UI-preferences document through a verified running Engine host; no confirmation, writes, migration, host start, pair listing or provider calls
commands.requires: a verified running Engine host; the current user's existing UI-preferences document

commands.effect: updates only explicitly supplied field paths/page keys in the current user's existing UI-preferences document through a verified running Engine host; requires a nonempty valid changed-field JSON patch and --yes, preserves unrelated fields, and returns committed merged preferences; no --pair, host start, local fallback, pair listing or provider calls
commands.requires: a verified running Engine host; exact explicitly supplied UI-preference field paths/page keys
